correctness.rationale: In a bipartition, the off-diagonal adjacency block B has rank m: a nonzero minor requires a matching, while the submatrix of a maximum matching has exactly one perfect matching (two would produce an alternating cycle). The negative eigenvalue count is rank B by the singular-value decomposition. The forest dominance complex has top reduced integral homology of rank one in degree m−1. For any maximum matching the oriented join of the endpoint differences embeds as a cycle: a closed neighborhood contains its vertex's matched edge or an unmatched vertex. By König's theorem a minimum cover has m vertices, one from each matched edge. It is a facet because each of its vertices has a neighbor outside it, and the outside is independent, so adjoining any outside vertex introduces its full closed neighborhood. Coefficient extraction at the cover facet vanishes on boundaries and has value s_M(C)=±1 on the matching cycle, proving that the cycle is primitive. Comparing the coefficients at C and gC gives the stated sorting-sign formula. Coordinate restriction of E_- to C is injective by negative definiteness (the complementary vertex set is independent), hence an isomorphism by dimension. If a cover replaces a by its matched partner b, the unique restricted basis vector supported at a on the old cover has quadratic form 2x_b<0: other neighbors of a must stay in both covers. The determinant sign therefore acquires the same reversal and row-order correction as s_M. The single-swap graph is connected: after contracting matching edges the unforced implications form a partial order on the matched-edge endpoint choices, since the contracted graph is a forest. One can change coordinates along that order to reach the coordinatewise meet of two admissible assignments, respecting all forced choices. Thus sign(d_C)/s_M(C) is constant. The natural restriction identity d_(gC) det(g|E_-)=s_g(C)d_C combines this with the integral coefficient formula. Isolated vertices are excluded from faces and E_-, disconnected components present no exception, and for m=1 the same proof gives the action on reduced H0.
residual_risks: The finite recorded 96-forest/344-action check uses numerical eigenspaces and samples at most five automorphisms per enumerated tree. It was not replayed and is not used to certify the infinite theorem; the exact proof is in RESULT.md lines 21–37.
The claim excludes m=0 and makes no stronger equivariant sphere-model or spectral-lattice assertion.

evidence: The forest theorem is nonequivariant. Its refinements give a labelled collapse and a generator associated to a maximal resolution, not an invariant spectral model. The inspected neighborhood/Alexander-duality work supplies general constructions but no negative determinant character. The catalogue fixed-space theorem is stronger on arbitrary subgroups' geometry, but computes the orientation by Euler characteristic rather than spectral or facet signs.

evidence: A known endpoint-difference generator makes extraction of a facet coefficient natural, but does not compare its transition signs to a negative definite adjacency restriction. The orbit formula does determine the same values, but passing to negative eigenspaces would need an additional argument: det(g|E_-)=(-1)^(m−dim(E_-)^<g>), and equality to the orbit formula requires identifying the invariant negative index with the matching number of the simple orbit forest. The invariant adjacency operator is weighted and can have a diagonal term from a flipped central edge; one cannot simply equate it with the simple adjacency matrix in the orbit theorem.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither the known homotopy type and generator nor the orbit-Euler formula omits merely a routine parameter substitution to get the asserted spectral bridge. The frozen proof supplies a separate mathematical comparison via all minimum covers and their determinant orientations.

originality.rationale: The sphere, its matching-number dimension, and the endpoint-difference generator technique are already established; the full topological sign also has a distinct indexed formulation via orbit-forest matching numbers. The supported distinct contribution here is the explicit identification with the determinant on the negative adjacency eigenspace for every forest, together with the arbitrary maximum-matching/minimum-cover coefficient comparison. The fixed-space record does not assert this spectral identification or the sorting formula; it is not evidence that the topology alone determines the spectral side without proof. No general publication-priority claim is made.
residual_risks: The targeted public search was unavailable, not negative evidence. An unindexed earlier spectral-orientation formula or a general result yielding it remains possible. The directly inspected sources distinguish the spectral bridge while establishing overlap in the topological character itself.

value.rationale: The orientation sign is the only nontrivial integral homology datum left after the classical sphere theorem, and the identification with a natural spectral subspace gives a structural bridge between two graph constructions for a whole class, including part-flipping actions and permutations of components. The exact minimum-cover recipe computes the same scalar without numerical diagonalization or a specially adapted matching. This is useful beyond either the nonequivariant sphere theorem or tabulating signs on a few trees, even though the orbit-forest formula also computes the topological sign.
residual_risks: Neither the comparison of orientation characters nor the cover recipe asserts an equivariant homotopy equivalence to the unit sphere in E_-.
